mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized indicates inflationary pressure, leading to potential monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL > 2% annualized does not correlate with negative 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500 in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which is indicative of economic strength and thus positive for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 5% does not correlate with positive 60-day forward returns for the S&P 500 in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases > 5% YoY does not correlate with positive 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500 in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment turns bearish.
failure_condition: If INDPRO < 12-month MA does not correlate with negative 5-day forward returns for the S&P 500 in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above the historical average and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > historical average AND CPIAUCSL rising
failure_condition: If the joint condition does not correlate with negative 60-day forward returns for the S&P 500 in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strong labor market conditions, which is positive for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the joint condition does not correlate with positive 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500 in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which is a positive signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases do not correlate with positive 60-day forward returns for the S&P 500 in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) below its 12-month moving average signals a contraction in economic activity, which is negative for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 < 12-month MA does not correlate with negative 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500 in more than 60% of instances.
